title: Could one use AI for a higher-end version of Jade Cocoon's fusion system?
author: tbok1992
selftext:
If you're unaware, Jade Cocoon was a mons game for PS1 with a unique system for how it fused monsters. Instead of using pre-made results ala games like Dragon Quest Monsters, it actually combined the textures/mesh into a wholly unique thing in real-time.

I'm not experienced with the tech of AI, just more curious about its capabilities, but could transformer AI be used to do a more advanced version of that with significantly higher-fidelity models? Like, combining their meshes/textures/rigging into one relatively cohesive package? I'm super curious!

comments.author: Big_Presentation2786
comments.body: You can use AI for whatever you want..

comments.author: Aesthetic-Engine
comments.body: Yes that's fairly easy to get a diffusion model to do that just upload 2 images and tell it to fuse them into one creature. You don't want to build a game around that though or you'd have to charge a monthly fee for your game to cover the API usage. Better to use AI to build an engine that does this reliably though probably not as polished-looking.

replies.author: Big_Armadillo_935
replies.body: Just run every combo through gpt-image-2, 5 times. 1.5cents per image.

replies.author: LeafyWolf
replies.body: Shit, I was paying 4 cent per image with Gemini flash API.

replies.author: Technical_Ad_440
replies.body: is that a 1k image though? nanao banana 2 is 10cents for a 2k image 16:9 that seems awfully cheap at 1.5 cents and ideally you want 4k

replies.author: Big_Armadillo_935
replies.body: 2k is ideal since a computer monitor is 4k max atm, and it is 1k generation but you can 2x an image with good results with offline ai upscalers like upscayle.

replies.author: Technical_Ad_440
replies.body: hmm havnt tried offline upscale nano banana feels like it fixes images when you upscale to so i feel like a 1k image upscale would come out messed up in comparison cause nano banana definitely fixes some small details on upscale but i will need to try i guess

replies.author: Big_Armadillo_935
replies.body: give it a shot, if it's a cartoon there is a different model builtin upscayle that handles it. there are different models for different art styles.

replies.author: TeeRKee
replies.body: Diffusion models are cheap to run locally. You don’t need a beefy hardware

comments.author: deadpool236o
comments.body: the jade cocoon system was essentially runtime mesh/texture blending, which modern tools handle differently. procedural generation engines like houdini can do geometry fusion at a technical level. for the visual/texture side of creature concepts before you build anything, Mage Space works well as a design iteration layer.
